decisions.reason: The delayed rollout, limited website prominence after launch, and the relatively high support burden of a specialized particle-therapy phantom suggest the option has largely revealed weak value and should be abandoned.
As a small-volume ionization chamber with dedicated visibility in the first two observed years, it fits the firm's core dosimetry line and is inexpensive to keep while demand uncertainty remains.
This chamber appears to be another core-line variant, and maintaining it preserves product-line breadth at modest cost while the market potential is still plausible.
A standard clinical ionization chamber is close to the firm's established business, so the product likely has steady strategic value and low incremental carrying cost.
Although more niche, a chamber for relative dosimetry complements the rest of the portfolio and is worth keeping open because the downside of waiting is limited.
A thimble ionization chamber is a conventional, complementary offering in medical dosimetry, making continued commercialization the lower-risk option.
